title: Adaptive kernel sampler + batch governor to reduce tail latency in continuous batching
creator: Maya Patel
description: Introduce an adaptive kernel sampling layer and a batch governor that jointly control admission and decode pacing to smooth continuous batching tail latency. The goal is a 30-50% reduction in 95/99th token latency for mixed short/long workloads without increasing median latency or token cost materially.
acceptance_criteria: 95th token latency reduction >= 30% on mixed production traces relative to baseline runtime-1.18
99th token latency reduction >= 20% with no increase in median latency > 5%
No regression (>1%) in token throughput for steady-state long-sequence workloads
Feature gated behind runtime flag and safe default off for Dedicated customers
Automated integration tests for admission path and kernel fallback cover both prefill and decode stages
decisions: Implement lightweight kernel cost estimator (kernel sampler) that probes per-shape expected execution time using sampled micro-benchmarks rather than full model evaluation
Batch governor will operate at the admission point: it manipulates slot reservation and introduces micro-delays to shape batch shapes to align with high-efficiency kernel choices
Prefill and decode pacing will be co-ordinated using a shared token-pace signal to avoid decode-induced microbursts
We will prefer conservative quantized kernels for admission when uncertainty > threshold; fall back to full-precision kernels when kernel sampler reports low latency variance
tradeoffs: Micro-probing increases small additional CPU overhead and a small number of synthetic kernel invocations — accepted to achieve better long-tail latency
Batch shaping by delaying a few ms can worsen individual request latency but reduces 95/99th across tenants — chosen due to overall SLA improvement
Conservative default gating for Dedicated and Private customers to avoid unexpected behavior in regulated environments
test_plan: Unit tests: kernel sampler accuracy mocks, admission gating logic paths
Integration tests: end-to-end traces replay with production traffic sampler (mixed prompt lengths)
Benchmarks: run on p4d and g5-class hardware with several model families (Llama-like, MPT, GPT-style) and with/without quantization profiles
Canary rollout: 1% of hosted traffic -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% with manual hold points tied to SLO dashboards
Chaos: simulate node preemption and kernel failure to validate fallback and rollback behavior
milestones: Kernel sampler prototype integrated into admission path (In Progress)
Batch governor policy engine + simple pacing controller (Planned)
E2E perf run and canary plan (Planned)

release_notes: Introduced an opt-in adaptive kernel sampler and batch governor to reduce long-tail token latency for mixed prompt length workloads. Disabled by default for Dedicated/Private customers.
Telemetry added: kernel_choice_reason, sampler_confidence, batch_shape_distribution, pacing_delay_ms
notes_for_rollout: Start with small canary (1%): measure 50/95/99th token latency and token throughput for affected routes
Monitor sampler_confidence histogram — if >80% low confidence, hold rollout
On fallback rate >2% for a sustained 15m window, toggle feature off automatically
Coordinate with capacity team to ensure probe CPU budget is available on canary cluster
